gaps.quote: The proposal is a conjecture about an upper-bound question
gaps.note: Wrong label. The conjecture that no algorithm runs in o(n log n) (equivalently, that n log n is an eventual lower bound c*n*lg n for every machine) is a lower-bound statement, not an upper-bound question. The paper (around line 379-382, 'Lower-bound scope') treats it as an eventual lower bound for every multiplication machine, whose negation needs one machine with liminf T(n)/(n lg n)=0. The page's own next clause (no algorithm can be faster) is a lower-bound claim, so the sentence is also internally inconsistent.
